transcript:
[Header]
Date: 2026-06-05
Time: 14:00 - 15:27 UTC
Duration: 87 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (PM), Marco (Eng), Leah (SRE), Devon (Tech Lead), Sam (Staff Eng)

[00:00] Aisha: ok, thanks everyone for joining, I'll kick us off, we have two main things today roadmap launch readiness and the incident review from last week. I know some folks have slides but we'll keep it conversational.
[00:22] Marco: yeah, I have the postmortem notes, can share screen after, quick note i think the autoscaler behavior compounded with the GPU memory leak, so we hit degraded throughput.
[00:38] Leah: right, and the alerts for KV cache evictions didn't fire as expected, the threshold was set to 95% and we pegged at 93 but eviction rate spiked, so the alert was noisy but didn't trigger.
[01:05] Devon: also noticed that the canary routing didn't failover to the warm pool, the routing rule expects exact model tag match, slight mismatch and we had partial traffic routed to slower fallback which increased p99.
[01:38] Sam: filler - uh, small clarification, when you say memory leak is it the runtime or the model binding?
[01:52] Marco: good q, looks like a runtime mem growth around continuous batching when sequences > 2k, probably our KV cache growth and not freeing keys, could be a GC path mismatch on quantized kernels.
[02:20] Aisha: easy follow up items then - Leah, can you add an alert for eviction rate, lower threshold and also add a runbook step to drain nodes?
[02:35] Leah: yep i'll do that, but i want to flag we need better telemetry on prefix cache hit rate, right now the dashboard is per-model not per-customer.
[02:50] Devon: for launch readiness, we need an explicit SLO matrix - p50/p95/p99 target, cost target per 1k tokens, and fallback policy. I have a draft canary playbook.
[03:13] Aisha: perfect, we should align that with Sales and Solutions, Sam can outreach?
[03:22] Sam: yep i'll sync with solutions and get the success criteria.
[03:30] [05:00] Aisha: ok, quick pause - we have a question from infra about dedicated pool sizing, Marco your thoughts?
[05:15] Marco: based on tail latency from last month we should reserve two extra nodes for burst, increase min replicas from 3 to 5 for peak hours, and tweak batcher to cap at 64 instead of 128 for 8k sequences. There's tradeoffs for unit cost.
[05:46] Leah: cost tradeoff is notable, but the SLA for enterprise customers requires <200ms p95 for short seqs, and brokers expect that. If we can't meet with hosted we offer Dedicated.
[06:10] Devon: note about private deployments - we saw a customer ask for on-prem KMS integration and audit field changes, we need a checklist before private launch. Who owns that?
[06:30] Aisha: security/compliance will own, but Product needs to provide required hooks. We'll create a ticket in JIRA.
[07:00] [10:00] Marco: back to incident, the sequence was: spike in long requests -> batcher growth -> cache eviction spike -> runtime mem growth -> node OOM -> autoscaler flapped -> partial routing to fallback model -> degraded p99 -> customer-visible errors.
[10:30] Leah: adding that the logs were ambiguous, some service names got munged in our observability, e.g., KV cache was transcribed in logs as K-V cash in a few entries which slowed triage.
[11:00] Sam: we should add synthetic load tests simulating 2% of traffic with long sequences to catch this in staging.
[11:15] Devon: agree, and run both on dedicated hardware and host to measure delta. Also want to test canary failover triggers.
[11:40] Aisha: ok action items then. Marco - adjust autoscaler and memory cgroup defaults, Leah - alert + runbook, Devon - canary plan, Sam - benchmark plan and customer success alignment. I'll draft the exec TL;DR.
[12:05] [20:15] Marco: about kernel selection for quantized kernels, we saw mismatch causing slower decode on T4 vs A100, need a matrix per hw arch. I can start a doc.
[20:40] Leah: put perf numbers per model family, i can help with traces from the profiler.
[21:05] Aisha: is SOC2 checklist impacting the launch? Security had a question about retention of request logs and embeddings.
[21:30] Devon: retention is configurable, but for the hosted product default is 30 days, for enterprise we offer longer retention with audit controls. For private deployments customer controls retention.
[22:00] Sam: client asked about VPC peering and split-tunnel, we'll need to document network patterns.
[22:20] Aisha: ok let's mark network docs as part of readiness.
[22:35] [30:00] Leah: on the topic of alerts, we should also add a runbook for degraded KV hit rate that includes immediate cach drain and scaling to prevent tail latencies.
[30:30] Marco: on the code side i'll add mem profiling endpoints and a nightly job to exercise long-sequence paths.
[31:00] Aisha: any objections to pausing the big model rollout until we have these in place?
[31:12] Devon: I'd prefer a limited canary to specific accounts with rollback policy rather than full pause.
[31:25] Sam: agree small canary is safer.
[31:40] [40:00] Aisha: ok, let's define canary gates: 1) alerting for eviction and memory, 2) autoscaler stable for 24h under synthetic load, 3) p99 under threshold or automatic fallback.
[40:30] Devon: and we'll add automatic model variant fallback when kernel mismatch detected.
[40:48] Marco: note on batching - we need to tune batcher heuristics based on sequence length distribution, we can send model-specific configs to the runtime, i'll prototype.
[41:20] Leah: SRE checklist for launch readiness: alerting, runbooks, pager rotas, escalation path, canary dashboards. I'll share template.
[41:45] Aisha: perfect.
[42:00] [50:00] (Incident review continued) Marco: root cause is multi-factor and we should update RCA doc, there's also a contributing factor of a bad release that changed KV eviction policy.
[50:20] Sam: do we have blame? i mean owner - who merged that change?
[50:35] Marco: change was in infra repo, PR by external contractor, it passed tests but not perf tests. We'll adjust CI to run a perf job in PRs touching cache code.
[51:00] Leah: and add guardrails in staging to prevent OOMs from reaching prod.
[51:20] Aisha: ok, timeline for fixes? small alerts + runbook within 72h, autoscaler + batcher tweaks within 1 week, canary plan within 10 days.
[51:40] [60:00] Devon: we should also prepare customer comms, a concise incident note and mitigation steps. I'll draft and Aisha will review.
[60:30] Sam: also coordinate with sales for any impacted customers and potential credits.
[60:50] [70:00] Aisha: recap - we've got assigned owners and due dates, next sync Friday. Any last comments?
[70:20] Marco: no, i'll open the PRs.
[70:35] Leah: i'll update the runbook.
[70:45] Devon: starting canary doc.
[71:00] Sam: i'll sync with solutions and ops.
[71:20] [86:00] Aisha: thanks all, i'll send the TL;DR and action items in email, meeting adjourned.

[Auto-summary]
